notes: A is the arguments of the example call `run(0.,0.,90.,90., 1., 100., 16, 16, [ [i/10. + 0.007, i/10. + 0.007, i/20.] for i in range(16) ])`. Changed for Q32: in A every town is moved by 0.007 rad in both coordinates. In the scaled upstream line the towns at (0, 0) and (1, 1) sit exactly on grid points, where acos(1 - eps) turns the ~1e-9 error of Q32 trigonometry into 0.28 km; now they are 51 and 63 km from the nearest grid point (still within range_ = 100 km), where acos amplifies that error by at most about 1 / sin(0.008) = 125. B is given too, built the same way (towns moved by -0.006 and +0.009 rad, weights by +0.01): its nearest towns are 49 and 69 km from a grid point, so B exercises the distance sum. A seeded perturbation of A moved every town by about 0.15 rad, left none within range_ and gave an all-zero output. B is the arguments of `run(0.,0.,90.,90., 1., 100., 16, 16, [ [i/10. - 0.006, i/10. + 0.009, i/20. + 0.01] for i in range(16) ])`.
